name: The Ship Inn

layers.essential_history: [[c:The Ship on West Street is an old coaching inn. Inns like this were busy when travellers and goods moved by horse and coach.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Oundle had many inns. The Rose and Crown on the Market Place dates from the 1600s.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:At the Ship, the potboy shows you a muddy handcart. Its wheels have left a trail of stone dust.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The handcart]]
material: [[c:The handcart belongs to Josiah Gant's inn.]]
[[c:Its wheels are white with stone dust, the same pale stone as Fotheringhay.]]
[[c:A splinter of carved oak is caught in the boards.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:What did the handcart carry? (one word)]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:The splinter of carved oak shows the handcart carried the oak crown.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Stuck? Take a hint: hints are free.]]

evidence: [[c:Josiah Gant's handcart has stone dust and a splinter of carved oak in it.]]
support: [[c:Support the town: the Ship is still a working pub.]]
directions_to_next: [[c:Head east, about 120 metres as the crow flies, to the war memorial.  Keep to pavements and public paths.]]
